chapter: Band family, war years and wrap-up
title: Draft board and the FBI agents in California
summary: Two men told him to return for induction and he made a train trip.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Right. What about the war years as a band leader? During World War 2, I mean.

Well, you know, I was, I played practically every camp base that you had during the war years. I left New York like when I was, when my "Greetings" were sent to me, I was in another city. I was on a one night tour.

Now, if I'm playing here today at the Concorde and tomorrow in Monticello, my "Greetings" would miss me about a day or two days. And when it caught up with me from New York, I was in California. And then, I'm, now they've got me.
I was, opened a club there for 8

weeks. So, when I played my first number, the club was full. I played the first number. Two gentlemen come up on the stand, right up with their hats on. I didn't know who they were. I didn't know one thing about FBI or nothing.

So, they said, 'Your name Erskine Hawkins?' I said yes. They said, 'Well, you've got to go back to New York.' Now, I haven't got it yet. I said, 'What's wrong?' They said, 'Your draft board's been trying to get hold of you. They sent us ahead to get you, to put you on a plane.' That was another thing. I had never been on a plane.

They've been trying to get you so you can come back and take your induction examination. I said, 'Well, I've been travelling.' They said we know. We've been missing you where you go, you know. And the thing about it while I was on this tour, if they got a base near where I'm playing, I would play a concert for that base, and then go 50, 100 miles from there and play the job that was booked for me through the office. And, I did that for quite a while.
So, I'll get back to the plane. I said well, I said okay. He said, 'What we'll do on the plane is make a reservation for you tomorrow morning on the plane at 5:00 so you can go back to New York.'

Now, I'm all, getting all shaky inside and everything. I said all right. But, be sure and be there on time. I said all right. I goes down to the plane the next morning and they come up to me at the bench. Now, you know, during this time, priority was for the Service. Planes, buses, and everything. So, they couldn't get me on that plane. And, I did a big sigh there. Breathed hard.
They said, 'Well, meet us at the train at 4:00. We'll have a berth for you.' So, I got there. I was 4:00, on the train. So, it took us, what, 2½ or 3 days to get back from there to New York.
